title: Dispatch CSA 6: Alderwick Hears Voices From the Calder Plain
summary: Openings have appeared far beyond the Institute grounds.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Residents of East Quay reported voices from empty rooms before sunrise yesterday. At the Mariners’ Rest, the proprietor heard his own voice giving an order he had not placed. Two streets away, a woman opened a wardrobe and saw shallow water beneath a motionless sky. The door shut when she dropped the handle.

Dr. Marr attributes the incidents to the Calder ranging anchor, which is still packed with the party in the Stratum. The Institute’s measurements suggest that the instrument has begun fixing routes merely by being carried close to the black stone. A return through the original aperture might carry those routes into Alderwick.

The younger party has been ordered to dismantle the anchor and return without it. Miss Bell replied that dismantling its outer frame would be straightforward; removing its central spindle might open every route it currently holds. “We need to know which passage is ours before we pull it,” she said.

The returned Miss Bell proposed an answer. With copper wire from her workshop, she built a small receiver that detects the difference between an object and what she calls its “anticipated position.” Yesterday she demonstrated it upon the two identical survey drums. One produced a clear note. The other gave a broken, wavering tone. Both drums were made in Alderwick. Only one has crossed the plain.

Miss Bell has asked to send the receiver through the Institute aperture. She admits that she does not remember building it during her expedition. “I know how because I have had six days to regret not having it,” she said. The Institute transmitted its construction drawings to the younger Miss Bell tonight.
